name: Amendments by the committee responsible – put to the vote collectively
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Directive 2003/87/EC as regards revised benchmark values for the heat and fuel benchmarks for the period from 2026 to 2030
section: Recital 2 | Recital 2 a (new) | Article 10a – paragraph 2b a (new)
part_text:
(2) To address concerns expressed by certain industrial sectors in the context of updating the benchmark values until 2030 and provide additional protection against the risk of carbon leakage, the quantity of allowances to be allocated for free for the period from 2026 to 2030, determined by the heat and fuel benchmarks (‘fallback benchmarks’), should be increased. In order to do so, it is appropriate to adjust the maximum annual update rate applied for the fallback benchmarks by using the totality of the allowances available for free allocation in the period from 2026 to 2030 as laid down in Commission Decision XXX [CSCF Decision], amounting to around 88 million allowances, as well as a third of the allowances that are not allocated in that period as a result of the reduction of free allocation under the third and fifth subparagraphs of Article 10a(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC, amounting to around 11 million allowances. Another third of those allowances, amounting to around 11 million allowances, should be transferred to the Modernisation Fund established under Article 10d of Directive 2003/87/EC and should be used to support investments, inter alia, in the modernisation of district heating systems. The last third should remain allocated to the Innovation Fund, established under Article 10a(8) of that Directive. The use of the additional allowances for free allocation corresponds to an indicative 12,5 % reduction to the fallback benchmarks compared to the values for the period from 2021 to 2025, namely an indicative average value heat and fuel benchmarks for the period from 2026 to 2030 of 41,4 and 37,3 allowances/TJ, respectively. In line with the targeted nature of this adjustment and the rules set out in in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 on the determination of the annual amount of allowances allocated for free to installations, the additional free allocation resulting from the adjustment should only concern the amounts determined by the fallback benchmarks. In specific cases, it is possible that the Union-wide ex-ante fuel benchmark do not adequately reflect the characteristics and emission performance of manufacturing processes within certain industrial sectors. Where significant discrepancies are clearly documented, sector-specific sub-benchmarks should be established to ensure that free allocation reflects the performance of the most efficient sub-installations within a sufficiently homogeneous peer group. To that end, with a view to already applying such sub-benchmarks during the period from 2026 to 2030, the Commission should establish as soon as possible, by means of implementing acts, the updated sub-benchmark values for the relevant subsector, giving priority to installations whose economic activities fall within NACE codes 23.20 and 23.31 set out in Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006. Those sub-benchmark values should be determined on the basis of the average greenhouse gas emission intensity of the 10 % most efficient installations in the respective sector, using the same reference period, dataset and methodology as the ex-ante fuel benchmark.

4 [please insert the full reference once available – CSCF Decision] / (2a) As a matter of principle, free allocation needs to be based on product benchmarks rather than inputs in order to maximise greenhouse gas emission reductions and energy-efficiency savings throughout the production process. It is therefore necessary to revise the rules for determining Union-wide ex-ante benchmarks, as the group of the 10 % most efficient installations might not be sufficiently representative of the sector or subsector concerned in all cases, having regard to the technologies used, the nature and scale of the activity, the share of production covered and the number of installations and sub-installations forming the basis of the benchmark.
